c-atoms.ie-n-o.key: Oxygen's fourth 2p electron is paired, and repulsion makes it easier to remove

c-imf.pentane.key: n-Pentane's long shape allows more contact, so stronger dispersion forces

c-imf.water-slope.key: Ice is less dense than liquid water, so raising pressure favors melting

c-imf.melting-heat.key: Overcomes intermolecular attractions, so the temperature stays constant

c-gas.real-vol.key: The molecules themselves occupy space that cannot be compressed

c-thermo.spont-rate.key: Nothing: spontaneity is thermodynamics, rate is kinetics

c-kin.catalyst.key: The activation energy (and so the rate), not ΔG or K

c-kin.arrhenius.key: A larger fraction of collisions have energy above the activation energy

c-kin.intermediate.key: An intermediate sits in an energy dip and can be detected; a transition state is a peak

c-eq.inert.key: No shift: the partial pressures of the reacting gases are unchanged

c-redox.salt-bridge.key: Lets ions flow to keep each half-cell electrically neutral

c-nuc.beta.key: A neutron becomes a proton and emits an electron; Z rises by 1

c-nuc.gamma.key: Only its energy: Z and A stay the same

c-nuc.mass-defect.key: Was released as binding energy, E = mc²

b-mol.peptide-planar.key: Planar and rigid, with partial double-bond character

b-mol.cellulose.key: Cellulose uses β(1→4) glycosidic bonds; starch uses α(1→4)

b-mol.saturated.key: Have no C=C double bonds, so they pack tightly and melt higher

b-mol.nucleotide.key: A phosphate group, a five-carbon sugar and a nitrogenous base

b-mol.denature.key: Secondary, tertiary and quaternary structure, not peptide bonds

b-cell.golgi.key: Modifies, sorts and ships proteins and lipids

b-cell.lysosome.key: Membrane sacs of hydrolytic enzymes that work best at acidic pH

b-cell.microtubule.key: Tubulin; the mitotic spindle, cilia and flagella

b-cell.endosym.key: They have their own circular DNA and bacteria-like ribosomes

b-mem.cholesterol.key: Buffers it: less fluid when warm, less stiff when cold

b-energy.ferment.key: To regenerate NAD⁺ so glycolysis can keep making ATP

b-energy.atp-synthase.key: Protons flowing down their gradient back into the matrix

b-energy.uncoupler.key: O₂ use continues, ATP synthesis falls, and heat is released

b-div.nondis-1.key: All abnormal: two with an extra chromosome, two missing one

b-div.nondis-2.key: Two normal gametes, one with an extra chromosome, one missing one

b-div.p53.key: Halts the cell cycle (at G₁/S) for repair or triggers apoptosis

b-dna.dnapol.key: 5′ → 3′, and only by extending an existing primer

b-dna.lagging.key: Polymerase only builds 5′→3′, so it must work away from the fork in short pieces

b-dna.rnapol.key: Reads the template 3′→5′ and builds RNA 5′→3′, with no primer

b-dna.processing.key: A 5′ cap, a 3′ poly-A tail and splicing out of introns

b-dna.codons.key: 64 codons; 61 code for amino acids and 3 are stops

b-dna.frameshift.key: Deleting one nucleotide from a coding sequence

b-dna.rna-dna.key: RNA has ribose (with a 2′-OH) and uracil instead of thymine

b-prok.plasmid.key: Small circular DNA molecules, separate from the chromosome

b-sys.rmp.key: K⁺ leaking out through open K⁺ channels

b-sys.repol.key: Na⁺ channels inactivate and voltage-gated K⁺ channels let K⁺ out

b-sys.refractory.key: Voltage-gated Na⁺ channels are inactivated and cannot reopen yet

b-sys.myelin.key: Signals jump between nodes of Ranvier (saltatory conduction)

b-sys.hormone-class.key: Steroids enter cells and bind intracellular receptors that alter transcription

b-sys.insulin.key: Lowers blood glucose by promoting cell uptake and glycogen synthesis

b-sys.adh.key: Inserts aquaporins in the collecting duct, increasing water reabsorption

b-sys.aldosterone.key: Increase Na⁺ reabsorption and K⁺ secretion

b-sys.pepsin.key: Digests protein in the stomach, activated from pepsinogen by acid

b-sys.pulm.key: The pulmonary artery, then the lungs

b-sys.cardiac.key: Striated, involuntary and joined by intercalated discs

p-kin.apex.key: Vertical velocity is zero, but acceleration is still g downward

p-mom.conserve.key: The net external force on the system is zero

p-mom.elastic.key: Both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved

p-mom.equilibrium.key: Net force is zero and net torque is zero

p-elec.dielectric.key: Capacitance rises and voltage falls (charge is fixed)

p-elec.meters.key: Ammeter in series (low resistance); voltmeter in parallel (high resistance)

p-light.tir.key: Light going from higher n to lower n, beyond the critical angle

p-light.violet.key: Shortest wavelength and highest photon energy

c-sep.vacuum.key: It lowers boiling points, so heat-sensitive compounds don't decompose

c-sep.ief.key: The pH equals its isoelectric point (net charge zero)

c-redox.conc-cell.key: E°cell = 0, but current flows until the concentrations become equal

b-signal.gq.key: PIP₂ is split into IP₃, which releases ER Ca²⁺, and DAG, which activates PKC

b-signal.rtk.key: Ligand brings receptor halves together; they phosphorylate each other's tyrosines

b-signal.amplify.key: Each step of the cascade activates many molecules of the next

b-signal.pde.key: It lasts longer, because cAMP is broken down more slowly

b-nerve.ipsp.key: Cl⁻ entering or K⁺ leaving, making the membrane more negative

b-nerve.ache.key: Prolongs acetylcholine's action, so stimulation lasts longer

b-nerve.reflex.key: Sensory neurons connect straight to motor neurons in the spinal cord

b-endo.thyroid-fb.key: High, because low thyroid hormone removes negative feedback

b-endo.cortisol.key: Raise blood glucose and suppress the immune response

b-endo.pth.key: Raises calcium through bone, kidney and vitamin D activation

b-circ.av.key: So the atria finish emptying into the ventricles before they contract

b-circ.fetal-hb.key: Binds O₂ more tightly, so it can take O₂ from the mother's blood

b-circ.s1.key: The AV valves closing as the ventricles start to contract

b-resp.inhale.key: The diaphragm contracts, chest volume rises and lung pressure drops

b-resp.hypervent.key: Respiratory alkalosis, from blowing off CO₂

b-resp.co.key: It binds hemoglobin far more tightly than O₂ does

b-resp.diffusion.key: Simple diffusion down its partial-pressure gradient

b-digest.trypsin.key: Enteropeptidase on the intestinal lining cleaves it to trypsin

b-digest.secretin.key: The pancreas to release bicarbonate-rich fluid

b-digest.glucagon.key: Stimulating glycogen breakdown and gluconeogenesis in the liver

b-immune.antibody.key: The variable regions at the tips of the arms

b-immune.clonal.key: An antigen activates the lymphocytes whose receptors already match it

b-muscle.troponin.key: Troponin, which shifts tropomyosin off actin's binding sites

b-muscle.ttubule.key: Carry the action potential deep inside to trigger Ca²⁺ release

b-muscle.smooth.key: Calmodulin, which activates myosin light-chain kinase

b-muscle.slow-twitch.key: Rich in mitochondria and myoglobin, and fatigue-resistant

b-muscle.calcitonin.key: Lower blood calcium by reducing bone resorption

b-repro.oogenesis.key: One egg, plus small polar bodies that degenerate

b-repro.arrest.key: Metaphase II, completing meiosis only if fertilized

b-repro.corpus.key: Progesterone, which maintains the uterine lining

b-repro.polyspermy.key: The cortical reaction, which hardens the zona pellucida

b-repro.cleavage.key: Divides into more, smaller cells without growing overall

b-evo.fitness.key: Leaves the most surviving, fertile offspring

b-evo.kin.key: Kin selection: helping relatives spreads shared genes

p-heat.isothermal.key: ΔU = 0, so the heat absorbed equals the work done

p-heat.second-law.key: Heat flows spontaneously from hot to cold, not the reverse

p-mag.no-work.key: Changes its direction but not its speed

p-atomic.intensity.key: Ejects more electrons without raising their maximum kinetic energy

p-atomic.absorption.key: The same wavelengths the gas emits when heated

p-atomic.fluorescence.key: Some energy is lost as heat before the photon is emitted

p-atomic.bohr.key: Energy levels are quantized, so only certain energy gaps exist
